transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-03-19 17:30 UTC | Duration ~52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonah Reed (Redwood SE), Priya Nair, Carlos Mendes, Ethan Park, Nina Gomez, Asha

[00:00] Maya: all right, everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood Inference — with me is Jonah our search lead. quick check audio — can you all hear us?
[00:10] Priya: yes loud and clear, thanks.
[00:15] Jonah: hi folks, i'll give a short demo of the hosted embeddings endpoint and then show how the reranker ties in via the /rerank endpoint, also a tiny Console tour for metrics.
[00:30] Carlos: great, quick context — we run a product search across ~12M SKUs, latency target is sub 150ms median, cost targets are tight, and we currently host vector indexes in-house.
[00:45] Jonah: got it. couple clarifying Qs — do you have a hard requirement for data residency or VPC-only?
[00:50] Priya: not strict, but some regulated customers need EU-only. also SSO + audit logs matter.
[00:58] Maya: Redwood hosted supports regional endpoints and we can do private-ish VPC peering on Dedicated later, but for a quick pilot hosted is easiest — we have SOC2 and we can share KMS options and audit logs.
[01:10] Ethan: yeah please send the SOC2 and KMS integration docs.
[01:15] Jonah: will do. ok demo — i'll share my screen, starting with Console: here's per-route token and latency breakdown, and the new embedding throughput panel. you can see recent perf of our small-quant model variant.
[01:35] [screen descriptions omitted, some audio overlap]
[01:50] Jonah: first step: embeddings call — POST /v1/embeddings with model redwood-embed-small, payload is text list, returns fixed-dim vectors. note: if you care about cost we show batch-ops and prefix caching that can save ~30%.
[02:10] Priya: when you say prefix caching do you mean KV cache for conversational contexts? we mostly do short queries but have repeated query patterns.
[02:18] Jonah: prefix/KV caching is mainly for generative KV cache but for embeddings you get batching + request-level caching — common queries will hit the cache if you opt in.
[02:28] Nina: any eyeballs on vector dimension sizes? we use 768 dims today.
[02:32] Jonah: our defaults support 256/512/768; higher dims cost more. for reranking we often take small-embed + cross-encoder reranker for final rank.
[02:40] Carlos: show the reranker flow.
[02:42] Jonah: sure — two-step: 1) retrieve top-k with similarity search (we demo with FAISS locally) using hosted embeddings; 2) POST candidates to /v1/rerank which runs a lightweight cross-encoder that scores passage vs query and returns final ordering. here's an example payload...
[02:58] [transcription glitch] "post candidates to slash vee one rerank" -> i.e. /v1/rerank
[03:05] Jonah: response includes score, token breakdown and latency. the Console traces route-level latencies so you can see embeddings time vs reranker time.
[03:18] Priya: what are typical latencies?
[03:20] Jonah: for a hosted small-embed + rerank pair we've seen p50 ~90ms for dense retrieval + rerank on optimized kernels when batch sizes small. p95 can be 200-350ms depending on sequence length for reranker.
[03:34] Priya: that's promising. our SLA target is p95 < 300ms.
[03:38] Jonah: doable with tuned batching and model variant selection. Optimize will recommend batch sizes and quantization profiles for cost vs latency.
[03:45] Carlos: how do we run AB tests on quality? can Redwood help with evals?
[03:48] Maya: yes, we have an eval harness, you can upload labelled datasets — Optimize will run regression tests and give quality deltas per-model. we'll share a spreadsheet template.
[03:58] [00:04:00] Ethan: security — how are payloads encrypted? do you persist raw queries?
[04:06] Maya: hosted persists short-term logs for debugging but you can opt out and pin retention. encryption in transit by TLS, at rest with KMS; for privacy-critical we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS.
[04:20] Priya: what about redaction for PII?
[04:23] Jonah: we offer pre-ingest redaction suggestions and you can run a sanitization step on our edge. not perfect but helps.
[04:30] [04:30] Jonah: live demo time — i'll call embeddings with a batch of 16 queries, sample response returns 768-d vectors, then a local FAISS run to get top-20, then call /v1/rerank with the 20 candidates.
[04:45] [screen noise and typing]
[05:10] Jonah: here's the rerank response — note scores look stable across repeated runs, Console shows token billing per call and suggested batching to reduce unit cost.
[05:25] Carlos: can we control model fallback? e.g. if capacity is constrained, can requests go to a cheaper model automatically?
[05:30] Maya: yes, smart routing policies let you route by latency or cost priority with automatic fallback to compatible variants. you can pin model versions too.
[05:40] Nina: any customer examples?
[05:42] Maya: a retail customer reduced cost 22% using Optimize's suggested quantization + batching while keeping MAP stable.
[05:50] [short pause / chime - user hands up]
[06:00] Priya: we want to run a 2-week pilot: 1) Redwood hosts embeddings and reranker in eu-west region, 2) we'll send 2k anonymized queries + labels, 3) Redwood will return baseline metrics and suggested config. is that fair?
[06:15] Maya: yes, pilot is great. i'll send the pilot doc and credits.
[06:20] Ethan: on pricing — what about per-token + per-rerank call?
[06:24] Maya: embeddings billed per-item vector + reranker billed per-request (and token accounting for reranker). i'll attach a sample pricing sheet.
[06:32] Carlos: one potential blocker: our legal needs to see data retention SLA and encryption proof.
[06:36] Maya: understood — i'll include SOC2 report, retention options, and KMS flow diagram.
[06:42] Priya: ok, timeline — we aim to start pilot next monday and have results in two weeks.
[06:46] Maya: great, we'll align on dates after you share the dataset.
[06:50] [06:50] Jonah: quick note on evals — we'll run ranking metrics (MRR, MAP, nDCG) and also surface qualitative failures in Console so you can probe.
[07:00] Carlos: can the reranker take additional signals like price or inventory flags?
[07:04] Jonah: yes the rerank call accepts metadata features per-candidate that the cross-encoder can consume in a lightweight fused vector. i'll send an example schema.
[07:12] Asha: (background) that's useful, echoing.
[07:18] [minor audio cut]
[07:22] Nina: what's the recommended vector store? you demoed FAISS; we use a managed vector DB.
[07:27] Jonah: any store that can export top-k works — we integrate with common DBs; for pilot simplest is to call hosted embeddings and run local FAISS for rerank. for production people use managed vector DB + Redwood reranker or pair with Dedicated.
[07:42] Priya: ok that's sensible.
[07:45] Maya: recap / next steps: i'll send pilot doc, pricing sheet, SOC2 + KMS diagrams; Jonah will post benchmark script and rerank example; Carlos will upload anonymized queries; schedule a security/deep-dive next week.
[07:58] Ethan: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:02] Maya: thank you all, we'll follow up.

End of transcript. Some timestamps approximate; occasional word substitutions typical of automated transcription (e.g., "rerank" transcribed as "rear rank" in spots).
